record.paper_title: Orthogonality Types in Normed Linear Spaces
record.original_question: For an arbitrary Carlsson orthogonality on a normed space X, defined by finite real coefficients a_i, b_i, c_i through an equation of the form sum_i a_i ∥b_i x + c_i y∥^2 = 0 under Carlsson's coefficient conditions, is uniqueness of that orthogonality equivalent to strict convexity of X?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.4 Is the uniqueness of any Carlsson orthogonality equivalent to strict convexity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a real normed linear space. A Carlsson orthogonality on $X$ is a binary relation $\perp_C$ defined by fixing a finite collection of real coefficients $\{a_i, b_i, c_i\}_{i=1}^n$ satisfying Carlsson's conditions
$$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i b_i^2 = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i c_i^2 = 0, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^n a_i b_i c_i = 1,$$
and declaring
$$x \perp_C y \iff \sum_{i=1}^n a_i\,\|b_i x + c_i y\|^2 = 0.$$
This family of relations includes Pythagorean orthogonality ($\|x\|^2 + \|y\|^2 = \|x+y\|^2$), isosceles orthogonality ($\|x+y\| = \|x-y\|$), and many others, and each Carlsson orthogonality coincides with the usual orthogonality whenever $X$ is an inner product space.

The orthogonality $\perp_C$ is called unique (on the right) if, for every $x, y \in X$, there exists exactly one real number $\alpha$ such that $x \perp_C (\alpha x + y)$.

The space $X$ is strictly convex if its closed unit ball is a strictly convex set; equivalently, $\|u+v\| < \|u\|+\|v\|$ whenever $u, v$ are nonzero and not positively proportional.

Question: For every Carlsson orthogonality $\perp_C$ on $X$ (i.e., for every admissible choice of coefficients $a_i, b_i, c_i$), is the uniqueness of $\perp_C$ on $X$ equivalent to the strict convexity of $X$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is known to hold in classical special cases: Pythagorean orthogonality is unique in every normed space, and isosceles orthogonality is unique if and only if the space is strictly convex (Dragomir–Kikianty, 2010). Recent papers (e.g., on 2-HH norm orthogonalities) continue to investigate uniqueness for specific Carlsson-type orthogonalities, but no general equivalence theorem covering all Carlsson orthogonalities has been located. The full equivalence for arbitrary Carlsson orthogonality appears to remain an open question.

status_evidence.title: On Uniqueness of New Orthogonality via 2-HH Norm in Normed Linear Space
status_evidence.snippet: Dragomir and Kikianty (2010) proved in their paper that the Pythagorean orthogonality is unique in any normed linear space, and isosceles orthogonality is unique if and only if the space is strictly convex.
status_evidence.claim: Known partial results exist for specific Carlsson orthogonalities (Pythagorean, isosceles), but a general equivalence theorem is not established.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonality in normed linear spaces (Carlsson)
status_evidence.snippet: Carlsson's original framework introducing the general family of orthogonality relations defined by sums of squared norms.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the Carlsson family of orthogonality relations underlying the question.
